original_question: Mutations in which gene cause the most common autosomal dominant form of spastic paraplegia?

final_qi.question: Mutations in which gene cause the most common autosomal dominant form of spastic paraplegia?
final_qi.long_answer: The most prevalent autosomal-dominant hereditary spastic paraplegia subtype, designated SPG4, arises from loss-of-function or missense mutations in the SPAST gene, which encodes the microtubule-severing ATPase spastin. SPAST mutations disrupt axonal microtubule dynamics, leading to the characteristic progressive lower-limb spasticity of dominant HSP.

final_answer.long_answer: The most frequent autosomal-dominant hereditary spastic paraplegia (designated SPG4) is caused by pathogenic variants in the SPAST gene, which encodes the microtubule-severing protein spastin. SPAST mutations account for about 40–50 % of autosomal dominant cases, making it the commonest genetic cause of this form of spastic paraplegia.
